An early payment discount is `a financial incentive offered by a seller to a buyer to encourage paying an invoice before the standard due date`.[[1]](https://www.allianz-trade.com/en_US/insights/early-payment-discount.html)[[2]](https://www.bdc.ca/en/articles-tools/money-finance/manage-finances/early-payment-discount-big-returns-business)

### Common Terminology

- **2/10 net 30:** The most common format. It means you receive a **2% discount** if you pay within **10 days** , otherwise the full balance is due in **30 days**.[[1]](https://www.bill.com/learning/early-payment-discounts)[[2]](https://www.papayaglobal.com/glossary/early-payment-discount/)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kTq9Ah56M4Q&t=60)
- **Alternative structures:** Can include fixed percentages, sliding scales, or dynamic discounting mechanisms managed through platforms like [Taulia](https://taulia.com/glossary/what-is-an-early-payment-discount/) or [Coupa](https://compass.coupa.com/en-us/products/product-documentation/supplier-resources/for-suppliers/coupa-supplier-portal/set-up-the-csp/financial-setup/early-payment-discounts).[[1]](https://www.allianz-trade.com/en_US/insights/early-payment-discount.html)[[2]](https://compass.coupa.com/en-us/products/product-documentation/supplier-resources/for-suppliers/coupa-supplier-portal/set-up-the-csp/financial-setup/early-payment-discounts)[[3]](https://www.papayaglobal.com/glossary/early-payment-discount/)

### Benefits for Each Party

- **For Buyers:** Lowers the total cost of goods and yields a high, risk-free return on cash.
- **For Sellers:** Accelerates incoming cash, reduces accounts receivable, lowers [NetSuite](https://www.netsuite.com/portal/resource/articles/accounting/early-payment-discount.shtml) days sales outstanding (DSO), and minimizes late payment risks.[[1]](https://taulia.com/glossary/what-is-an-early-payment-discount/)[[2]](https://www.bdc.ca/en/articles-tools/money-finance/manage-finances/early-payment-discount-big-returns-business)[[3]](https://www.allianz-trade.com/en_US/insights/early-payment-discount.html)[[4]](https://www.netsuite.com/portal/resource/articles/accounting/early-payment-discount.shtml)

### How to Evaluate the Value

- **Calculate annualized return:** A 2% discount paid 20 days early on a 30-day term equals an annualized return of roughly 36% to 37%.
- **Compare to cost of capital:** If the annualized return of taking the discount beats your business's borrowing rate or alternate cash yield, taking the discount is typically worth it.[[1]](https://melio.com/blog/early-payment-discounts/)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KxFMjlzPU2E)[[3]](https://www.bill.com/learning/early-payment-discounts)

A **reorder point (ROP)** is `the specific inventory level that triggers a new order to your supplier so your stock arrives right before you run out`.[[1]](https://www.netsuite.com/portal/resource/articles/inventory-management/reorder-point-rop.shtml)[[2]](https://www.agrinventory.com/blog/reorder-point-definition-formula/)

### The Formula

Reorder Point=(Average Daily Usage×Lead Time in Days)+Safety Stock Reorder Point equals open paren Average Daily Usage cross Lead Time in Days close paren plus Safety Stock R e o r d e r P o i n t=(A v e r a g e D a i l y U s a g e×L e a d T i m e i n D a y s)+S a f e t y S t o c k  

- **Average Daily Usage:** The number of units you sell or use on a normal day.
- **Lead Time:** The number of days it takes for your supplier to process and deliver your new order.
- **Safety Stock:** Extra buffer inventory kept on hand to protect against unexpected shipping delays or sudden spikes in customer demand.[[1]](https://www.zoho.com/inventory/academy/inventory-management/what-is-a-reorder-point.html)[[2]](https://www.letsbloom.com/calculators/reorder-point/)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LLKG2bs-HlA)[[4]](https://www.inflowinventory.com/blog/reorder-point-formula-safety-stock/)

### An Example

- You sell **50 bags** of coffee beans a day.
- Your supplier takes **5 days** to deliver a new shipment.
- You keep a buffer of **100 bags** as safety stock.[[1]](https://www.sage.com/en-us/blog/reorder-point-why-is-it-important-for-managing-inventory/)

ROP=(50×5)+100=350 bags ROP equals open paren 50 cross 5 close paren plus 100 equals 350  bags R O P=(5 0×5)+1 0 0=3 5 0 b a g s When your inventory drops down to **350 bags** , you immediately place a new order.[[1]](https://www.sage.com/en-us/blog/reorder-point-why-is-it-important-for-managing-inventory/)

### Why It Matters

- **Prevents Stockouts:** You never run completely out of goods and lose sales.
- **Reduces Holding Costs:** You do not order too early and tie up cash in excess warehouse inventory.[[1]](https://acctivate.com/what-is-a-reorder-point/)[[2]](https://www.netsuite.com/portal/resource/articles/inventory-management/reorder-point-rop.shtml)[[3]](https://www.agrinventory.com/blog/reorder-point-definition-formula/)

A **PAR (Periodic Automatic Replacement)** level is `the minimum quantity of an item a business must keep in stock to meet customer demand until the next delivery arrives`.[[1]](https://www.fishbowlinventory.com/blog/par-level)

### Common Formulas

Depending on how your business tracks deliveries, you can calculate your PAR level using one of two standard methods:[[1]](https://www.brightpearl.com/blog/par-level-inventory-management)

- **Daily Sales & Lead Time Method:**   
`PAR Level = (Average Daily Sales × Lead Time in Days) + Safety Stock`   
*(Lead time is how many days it takes for a new order to arrive; safety stock is an extra buffer for unexpected spikes or delays).* 
- **Weekly Usage & Deliveries Method:**   
`PAR Level = (Weekly Inventory Usage + Safety Stock) ÷ Deliveries per Week` [[1]](https://www.unleashedsoftware.com/blog/par-levels-in-inventory-management-with-formula-examples/)[[2]](https://www.brightpearl.com/blog/par-level-inventory-management)[[3]](https://flexscanmd.com/blog/how-to-create-inventory-par-levels/)



---

### How Ordering Works

- **The Order Quantity:** To figure out how much to buy, subtract your current stock on hand from your PAR level:  
`Order Quantity = PAR Level − Current Stock` [[1]](https://www.unleashedsoftware.com/blog/par-levels-in-inventory-management-with-formula-examples/)
- **PAR vs. Reorder Point:** A PAR level defines the *target quantity* you want to reach, whereas a reorder point is the specific low-water mark that *triggers the timing* to place the order.[[1]](https://www.fishbowlinventory.com/blog/par-level)[[2]](https://www.brightpearl.com/blog/par-level-inventory-management)



---

### Where It Is Used

- **Restaurants & Hospitality:** Manages perishable ingredients, reduces food waste, and prevents 86'ing menu items. Guides are available via platforms like [Restaurant365](https://www.restaurant365.com/blog/restaurants-par-levels/).[[1]](https://www.unleashedsoftware.com/blog/par-levels-in-inventory-management-with-formula-examples/)[[2]](https://supy.io/blog/what-is-par-level-how-to-calculate-par-level)[[3]](https://www.restaurant365.com/blog/restaurants-par-levels/)
- **Healthcare & Pharmacies:** Ensures critical medical supplies, drugs, and equipment are always ready for patient care.[[1]](https://study.com/academy/lesson/par-level-system-definition.html)[[2]](https://www.unleashedsoftware.com/blog/par-levels-in-inventory-management-with-formula-examples/)
- **Retail & Vending:** Keeps shelves stocked without tying up excess cash, using tools such as [Parlevel Systems](https://www.parlevelsystems.com/) for automated tracking.[[1]](https://www.parlevelsystems.com/)[[2]](https://www.fishbowlinventory.com/blog/par-level)

Landed cost is `the total financial expense of delivering a product from the factory or seller's door to the final destination`.[[1]](https://www.dhl.com/discover/en-global/logistics-advice/essential-guides/landed-cost-meaning-formula-calculation)

### Key Components

- **Product Price:** The cost of raw materials, manufacturing, and the supplier's margin.
- **Freight and Shipping:** Inland transport, ocean or air freight, and last-mile delivery fees.
- **Customs and Duties:** Tariffs, import/export fees, merchandise processing fees, and harbor maintenance fees.
- **Insurance:** Cargo coverage protecting against lost, stolen, or damaged goods.
- **Overhead and Risk:** Currency exchange rate fluctuations, payment processing fees, and port storage or demurrage charges.[[1]](https://www.fedex.com/en-us/small-business/articles-insights/what-is-landed-cost.html)[[2]](https://www.dhl.com/discover/en-global/logistics-advice/essential-guides/landed-cost-meaning-formula-calculation)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/Z3uP8XOOAKc)[[4]](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/netsuite/ns-online-help/section_N2417056.html)[[5]](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/hDxn_T_ze1E)

### Basic Formula
\text{Landed Cost} = \text{Product Cost} + \text{Shipping/Freight} + \text{Customs & Duties} + \text{Insurance} + \text{Overhead/Handling}  
To get the **unit landed cost** , divide the total landed cost of the entire shipment by the total number of units.[[1]](https://www.wtagroup.com/resources-and-insights/blogs/why-total-landed-costs-need-to-be-considered)

### Why It Matters

- **Accurate Pricing:** Prevents businesses from underpricing items and losing profit margins to hidden fees.
- **Supplier Comparisons:** Allows you to weigh a cheap overseas supplier with high shipping/tariff costs against a more expensive local vendor.
- **Inventory Valuation:** Essential for proper accounting and tracking true stock values in systems like NetSuite Applications Suite or specialized guides by [FedEx](https://www.fedex.com/en-us/small-business/articles-insights/what-is-landed-cost.html) and [DHL Express](https://www.dhl.com/discover/en-global/logistics-advice/essential-guides/landed-cost-meaning-formula-calculation).[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/Z3uP8XOOAKc)[[2]](https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/netsuite/ns-online-help/section_N2417056.html)[[3]](https://www.fedex.com/en-us/small-business/articles-insights/what-is-landed-cost.html)[[4]](https://www.dhl.com/discover/en-global/logistics-advice/essential-guides/landed-cost-meaning-formula-calculation)

### Key Components

- **Average Daily Usage:** The number of units you sell or use per day, calculated over a recent period (such as the last 90 days).
- **Average Lead Time:** The number of days it takes for your supplier to deliver a new order, from the moment you place it until it is ready to sell.
- **Safety Stock:** Extra buffer inventory kept on hand to protect against unexpected demand spikes or delivery delays.

A landed cost is the total expense of delivering a product from the supplier to your final warehouse or customer , combining the purchase price with all shipping, compliance, and import fees.[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mlqWKkhgBik&vl=en&t=16)[[2]](https://endlesscommerce.com/tools/landed-cost-calculator)

### The Landed Cost Formula

\text{Total Landed Cost} = \text{Product Cost} + \text{Shipping & Freight} + \text{Insurance} + \text{Customs Duties & Tariffs} + \text{Import Taxes/VAT} + \text{Brokerage & Handling Fees}

To find the cost for a single item:  
Landed Cost per Unit=Total Landed Cost Number of Sellable Units Landed Cost per Unit equals the fraction with numerator Total Landed Cost and denominator Number of Sellable Units end-fraction L a n d e d C o s t p e r U n i t=T o t a l L a n d e d C o s t N u m b e r o f S e l l a b l e U n i t s



---

### What Each Component Includes

- **Product Cost:** The supplier’s invoice price, including packaging, tooling, or custom modifications.
- **Shipping & Freight:** Origin transportation, international air/ocean freight, port fees, and inland delivery to your warehouse.
- **Insurance:** Coverage protecting the cargo while in transit.
- **Customs Duties & Tariffs:** Government taxes assessed based on your product's **Harmonized System (HS) code** and country of origin.
- **Taxes & Government Fees:** Value-Added Tax (VAT), Merchandise Processing Fees (MPF), or Harbor Maintenance Fees (HMF).
- **Brokerage & Handling:** Customs broker fees, port terminal handling, inspection costs, and currency conversion buffers.[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_VK5wMdG9hg)[[2]](https://www.icontainers.com/calculator/landed-cost-calculator/)[[3]](https://passportglobal.com/blog/landed-cost-calculator-how-to-calculate-total-import-costs/)[[4]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mlqWKkhgBik&vl=en&t=16)[[5]](https://www.sequenzy.com/tools/landed-cost-calculator)
